item.title: Sonos Plans ‘Ace Ultra’ Headphones and Broad Push Into AI
item.description: Sonos Inc. is readying a new pair of wireless headphones, the first product in an upcoming hardware wave that will see the audio company push deeper into artificial intelligence and frame its signature whole-home system as an ideal match for cutting-edge AI models and voice interactions.

item.title: AI Data Center Boom Is ‘Maxing Out’ P&C Insurers, AIG CEO Says
item.description: American International Group Inc. Chief Executive Officer Eric Andersen said that while the artificial intelligence buildout presents a “great opportunity” for the insurance industry, it’s also pushing property and casualty providers to their limits.

item.title: Barclays Sees Picky Bond Buyers Keeping Yields at Multiyear Peak
item.description: A shift in the buyer base of US Treasuries toward value-oriented mutual funds, households and other private investors has helped propel 30-year yields to multi-decade peaks, according to Barclays Plc.

item.title: OpenAI Executive Brad Lightcap Leaves to ‘Start Something New’
item.description: OpenAI executive Brad Lightcap is leaving the artificial intelligence company to start a new project, months after he stepped away from his role as chief operating officer.

item.title: SEC Weighs Direct Funding for Costly Market-Tracking Database
item.description: The Securities and Exchange Commission is considering taking direct control of a controversial database that tracks trades across US equities and options markets after Citadel Securities won a lawsuit challenging its funding last year.

item.title: A Solar Eclipse Will Flip the Off Switch on Europe’s Solar Farms
item.description: Night will fall on Europe’s power system a bit early Wednesday evening, as an eclipse is set to block solar generation across parts of the UK and western Europe.

item.title: Radiant World Offers $150 Million Aluminum Stash for Sale
item.description: Metals trader Radiant World has been seeking to sell a stockpile of aluminum worth some $150 million at a small discount to market prices in an attempt to boost its liquidity, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Nvidia Credit Risk Eases After CEO Clarifies $500 Billion Plan
item.description: Bond traders dialed back measures of credit risk associated with Nvidia Corp. on Tuesday after the company said it would limit its exposure in a $500 billion plan to finance the type of artificial-intelligence investments that are driving demand for its computer chips.

item.title: JBS Seeks US Margin Recovery With New CEO Pledging Continuity
item.description: JBS NV said its main business of US beef is yet to benefit from a restructuring plan, but sees that effort as well as a renewed flow of Mexican cattle eventually aiding meatpacking margins.

item.title: Latvia’s Air Baltic Plans Smaller Fleet, Debt-for-Equity Swap
item.description: Air Baltic Corp has outlined a plan to turn around the ailing business by cutting costs and swapping much of its existing bond for equity.

item.title: US Opens In-Depth Antitrust Review of Kone-TK Elevator Deal
item.description: The US Justice Department is investigating Kone Oyj’s €29.4 billion ($34.4 billion) purchase of rival TK Elevator, putting pressure on a deal that would create the largest elevator manufacturer in the world.

item.title: Manus to Resume Independent Operations in Unwind of Meta Deal
item.description: The Chinese-founded artificial intelligence startup Manus said it would soon resume operating as an independent company, the latest step in efforts to unwind its purchase by Meta Platforms Inc. after government authorities in China blocked the transaction.

item.title: Trend-Chasing Funds’ Big Short on Bonds Raises Stakes for CPI
item.description: Record short bets against global bonds by trend-chasing investors are lifting the stakes for US inflation reports this week.

item.title: Blue Owl Set to Raise $750 Million to Pay Down Credit Lines
item.description: Blue Owl Capital Inc. is selling $750 million of high-grade debt, up from initial discussions of $500 million, after receiving a large amount of investor orders, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Chicago Mayor Demands Data Center Moratorium After Backlash
item.description: Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson is pushing for a temporary moratorium on data centers, and signed an executive order on Tuesday to create new rules for any future developments.

item.title: Phia App Co-Founders Pushed for Features Taking Credit for Sales It Didn’t Drive
item.description: Phia co-founders Phoebe Gates and Sophia Kianni pushed for features in the e-commerce startup’s software that took credit for sales it didn’t drive, according to internal communications and people with knowledge of the matter.

item.title: Russia Budget Gap Spikes Despite Oil Windfall Driven by Iran War
item.description: Russia’s budget gap sharply widened despite a windfall in energy revenue driven by the tensions around the Strait of Hormuz, as the Kremlin continues to ramp up spending on its war in Ukraine.

item.title: US Household Delinquencies Improve: NY Fed Quarterly Report
item.description: The share of overdue consumer loans fell slightly in the second quarter, and so did some measures of newly delinquent debt, pointing to improvements for the US consumer.

item.title: Activist Anson Funds Pushes Lionsgate for Sale, Semafor Says
item.description: Activist investor Anson Funds Management is urging Lionsgate Studio Corp. to put itself up for sale, Semafor reported, adding to pressure on the independent film and TV production company to do a deal.

item.title: Kenya Joins Peers in Leaving Interest Rates on Hold on Iran War
item.description: Kenya’s central bank kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged for third time in a row as it monitors the impact of the ongoing Iran war on the economy.

item.title: Atlanta Airport Taps Munis for $1.1 Billion as Sector Sales Lag
item.description: The world’s busiest airport is coming to market with a more than $1 billion municipal bond sale, boosting issuance in the lagging airport sector.

item.title: MTN Sees First-Half Profit Jump on Nigeria, Ghana Mobile Gains
item.description: MTN Group Ltd. said adjusted first-half earnings climbed as much as 23% after improved results from the Nigerian, Ghanaian and Ugandan operations of Africa’s biggest mobile-network operator.

item.title: Chobani Cuts Annual Earnings Forecast on Rising Material Costs
item.description: Chobani has lowered its annual earnings forecast as the Greek yogurt maker contends with rising material costs, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: CSN Gets Financial Relief as $1 Billion Debt Exchange Approved
item.description: Brazil’s Cia. Siderurgica Nacional SA got enough support from holders to push through a debt exchange, getting it fresh financial relief as it struggles to cope with high financing costs.

item.title: US Previously Owned Home Sales Decline to Three-Month Low
item.description: US sales of existing homes fell to a three-month low in July as elevated prices and mortgage rates continued to weigh on the housing market.

item.title: Russia’s Crude Oil Exports Tumble to Their Lowest Since May
item.description: A brief lull in drone strikes allowed refiners to boost runs, likely diverting crude from exports

item.title: NYSE Parent ICE Looks to Raise About $3.5 Billion From Bond Sale
item.description: Intercontinental Exchange Inc. has begun the sale of US investment-grade bonds two weeks after announcing a $6 billion deal to acquire MarketAxess Holdings Inc.

item.title: Severe Thunderstorms Across US Midwest Trigger Flood Warnings
item.description: The US Midwest and Ohio Valley, including Chicago and Cincinnati, face an enhanced, or level 3, risk of severe thunderstorms.

item.title: Defense Startup Neros Triples Valuation to $2.5 Billion
item.description: Neros Inc. raised $250 million in a funding round that tripled its valuation to $2.5 billion, money that will boost the defense startup’s drone development and production to meet rising US government demand.

item.title: South Africa Vows Eskom Won’t Weaken After Transmission Restructuring
item.description: South Africa’s presidency rebuked the chairman of Eskom Holdings SOC Ltd. for publicly questioning the plan to restructure the state power utility.
